items.title: Buster Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: I mean some of the albums that I have that you’re on, with Joe Farrell and those CTI

ctx.x: about the fact that the singers, you know you’re playing the same thing over and over again. He said, “Anytime that you’re able to have your instrument in your hand is a moment of reverie.” And he said, “If your responsibility tonight is to do nothing but play one whole note C, play it better tonight than you played it last night, with the resolve that you’ll play it better tomorrow than you play it tonight.” And he used to make me — he would allow no slack in my left hand. When my hands would hurt, my fingers…

Well it worked, for sure. I mean some of the albums that I have that you’re on, with Joe Farrell and those CTI — you’ve got this thing happening, it’s just so great. I mean congratulations I guess is all I can say, it’s great. Do you have a discography of all the things you’ve played on over the years?
You know at my web site, if you go to my recording page there’s a discography there, you can click on it and it stretches out.
